questionText:
Consider two relations describing teams and players in a sports league:

  • teams(tid, tname): tid, tname are team-id and team-name, respectively
  • players(pid, pname, tid): pid, pname, and tid denote player-id, player-name and the team-id of the player, respectively

Which ONE of the following tuple relational calculus queries returns the name of the players who play for the team having tname as 'MI'?
options: { p.pname | p \in players \land \exists t (t \in teams \land p.tid = t.tid \land t.tname = 'MI') }
{ p.pname | p \in teams \land \exists t (t \in players \land p.tid = t.tid \land t.tname = 'MI') }
{ p.pname | p \in players \land \exists t (t \in teams \land t.tname = 'MI') }
{ p.pname | p \in teams \land \exists t (t \in players \land t.tname = 'MI') }
explanation:
To get the names of players who play for the team with $tname = 'MI'$, we need to:
1. Select tuples $p$ from the $players$ relation ($p \in players$).
2. Select the player's name attribute ($p.pname$).
3. Ensure there exists a tuple $t$ in the $teams$ relation ($t \in teams$).
4. Join both relations using the common attribute $tid$ ($p.tid = t.tid$).
5. Apply the filter for the team name ($t.tname = 'MI'$).

Correct Formula:
$\{ p.pname \mid p \in players \land \exists t (t \in teams \land p.tid = t.tid \land t.tname = 'MI') \}$

Therefore, Option (A) is correct.
